notes.title: Steam Audio Open Source Release
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/27920370/bda009725ee7f228e1cb9d3c70dec29f0b89bdae.png[/img]
We are excited to announce that with the [url=https://github.com/ValveSoftware/steam-audio/releases]latest release of Steam Audio[/url], the complete source code of the Steam Audio SDK is now available as open source. With this release, our goal is to provide more control to developers, which will lead to better experiences for their users, and hopefully valuable contributions back to the wider community of developers using Steam Audio.

This comes after receiving a lot of valuable feedback and contributions from the community to the plugins already available as open source (Unity, Unreal, and FMOD Studio), and we want to bring those same benefits to the core SDK. This will allow developers to tailor the SDK to their needs, and deliver improved experiences to everyone using the technology. We will also continue our ongoing work on Steam Audio, including the release of bug fixes and new features.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/27920370/5f953809052eaec29095ebc8137222ac7833f640.png[/img]
The choice of what features we work on is often driven by the needs of internal projects. For instance, during the development of Half-Life: Alyx, we spent a lot of time working on our [url=https://steamcommunity.com/games/596420/announcements/detail/2979678779862082472]hybrid reverb and pathing features[/url], which we later released as part of Steam Audio 4.0.0. These priorities might not always align with partner priorities, so we want to remove roadblocks that prevent partners from implementing spatial audio features that require access to the core Steam Audio SDK. As an example, we may be working on fixing a performance issue in Steam Audio affecting an internal project, but a partner may need Steam Audio ported to a console platform. Making the entire SDK available as open source allows partners to manage the port themselves, and optimize it for their needs, while also allowing them to contribute their changes back if desired.

The [url=https://github.com/ValveSoftware/steam-audio]entire Steam Audio codebase[/url], including both the SDK and all plugins, is now released under the [url=https://choosealicense.com/licenses/apache-2.0/]Apache 2.0 license[/url]. This allows developers to use Steam Audio in commercial products, and to modify or redistribute it under their own licensing terms without having to include source code. We welcome contributions from developers who would like to fix bugs or add features to Steam Audio; for more details, see the files [url=https://github.com/ValveSoftware/steam-audio/blob/master/LICENSE.md]LICENSE.md[/url] and [url=https://github.com/ValveSoftware/steam-audio/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md]CONTRIBUTING.md[/url] in the GitHub repository.

notes.title: Steam Audio 4.1.0 Release
notes.notes:
We've just released [url=https://valvesoftware.github.io/steam-audio/downloads.html]Steam Audio 4.1.0[/url]. This release includes a major update to the Steam Audio Unreal Engine plugin, bringing it up to date with the latest features of the Steam Audio SDK. This is also the first release in which the Unreal Engine plugin is released alongside the other plugins and the core SDK.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/27920370/9f293b279c8f8711bbdbe67cbce8f220b9a71d4d.png[/img]

The major new features of the Unreal Engine plugin in this release include:

[h3]FMOD Studio support[/h3]
If you are using FMOD Studio as your audio middleware in your Unreal Engine project, the Steam Audio Unreal Engine plugin now works with the Steam Audio FMOD Studio plugin. Events authored in FMOD Studio can use occlusions, reverb, etc. simulated by Steam Audio in Unreal Engine levels.

[h3]macOS and Linux support[/h3]
The Unreal Engine plugin now supports Windows (64-bit Intel), macOS (64-bit Intel), Linux (64-bit Intel), and Android (32-bit ARM, 64-bit ARM, and 32-bit Intel). Note that precompiled macOS binaries are not provided out of the box, but Unreal Engine will automatically compile the plugin for macOS when you open a project that uses the plugin. Precompiled binaries for macOS will be provided in a subsequent patch release.

[h3]Sublevel support (including streaming sublevels)[/h3]
Geometry can be tagged in any sublevel referenced by a level. Whether the sublevels are loaded automatically along with the main level, or streamed in based on a level streaming volume or any custom logic, Steam Audio will update occlusion, reflections, and reverb automatically.

[h3]Dynamic geometry in Blueprint classes[/h3]
Any Blueprint class can now be configured to be a Steam Audio dynamic object, and Steam Audio will automatically update occlusion, reflections, and reverb as instances of the Blueprint class move through your levels.

[h3]Baked data exported to .uassets[/h3]
Level geometry (both static and dynamic) as well as baked sound propagation data is now stored in .uasset files that are referenced by Steam Audio components. This simplifies the packaging workflow for your projects.

[h3]Latest Steam Audio SDK features[/h3]
In addition to the above, this release of the Steam Audio Unreal Engine plugin includes all the latest features of the core Steam Audio SDK, such as pathing, hybrid reverb, and more.

Going forward, updates to the Unreal Engine plugin will continue to be available on GitHub, including source code and pre-built binaries. The version of Steam Audio built into Unreal Engine will be periodically updated, but the latest versions will always be available on GitHub.

For the full release notes for this release, click [url=https://github.com/ValveSoftware/steam-audio/releases/tag/v4.1.0]here[/url].

notes.title: Steam Audio 4.0.0 Release
notes.notes:
We've just released [url=https://github.com/ValveSoftware/steam-audio/releases/tag/v4.0.0]Steam Audio 4.0.0[/url], which is a major update to Steam Audio. This release includes new features and an updated API that is more flexible than previous releases. Because this is a major update, the version numbering we used so far was no longer sufficient: we have updated from 2.0-beta.20 (the previous release) to 4.0.0 (the next available integer).

This release includes features that were developed or significantly enhanced during the development of [i]Half-Life: Alyx[/i].

[url={STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/27920370/6213f1376bb7220170254ce0fcc8c81c5a1ff03b.png][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/27920370/6213f1376bb7220170254ce0fcc8c81c5a1ff03b.png[/img][/url]

The major new features in this release include:

[h3]Pathing[/h3]
Pathing is a new way of baking sound propagation from a moving source to a moving listener. This involves placing probes in the scene, and calculating shortest paths between each pair of probes. At run-time, this baked data is used to calculate how sound propagates from the moving source to the moving listener, and spatialize the sound accordingly. If a baked shortest path is occluded by dynamic geometry (like a door), Steam Audio can recalculate alternate shortest paths on the fly. Steam Audio also applies a diffraction model to paths that bend around corners or through doorways, etc. This feature is useful for modeling how sound emitted by an occluded source reaches the player through doors or windows instead of directly through walls.

[h3]Hybrid Reverb[/h3]
When rendering reflections or reverb, Steam Audio can use convolution reverb (which is defined in terms of an impulse response) or parametric reverb (which is defined in terms of a small set of parameters, like decay time). Convolution reverb results in more accurate reproduction of early reflections and directionality, but requires more CPU. Parametric reverb requires less CPU, but cannot reproduce early reflections as accurately, especially in outdoor spaces. Hybrid reverb is a hybrid of the two: the early reflections are rendered using an impulse response, and the later reverb tail is rendered using parametric reverb. The transition between the two types of reverb is smooth and controllable, as is the length of the reverb tail. This feature is useful for trading off reverb quality and performance.

[h3]Unity Plugin: Additive Scenes[/h3]
The Unity plugin now has full support for additive scenes. Multiple scenes can be opened additively in the editor, and exported separately. Scenes can be additively loaded and unloaded freely at run-time, and Steam Audio will automatically update occlusion, reflections, and pathing simulation to account for the changes.

[h3]C API Redesign[/h3]
The Steam Audio C API has been significantly redesigned, with the goal of increasing the flexibility available to developers and sound designers. Developers can control when and how often simulations are run, and can perform arbitrary post-processing before using the simulation results for rendering. For example, after simulating reverb, the length of the reverb tail can be increased or decreased based on the game state. Simulation results can also be used outside of spatial audio rendering: for example, the results of pathing simulation can be used to drive enemy AI.

Due to the major changes in the API and plugin design, this release is not backwards-compatible with previous releases. In-place upgrades are not recommended for existing projects, except those in the earliest stages of development.

This release includes updates to the Unity plugin, FMOD Studio plugin, and C API. An update to the Unreal plugin will be released separately.

For the full release notes for this release, click [url=https://github.com/ValveSoftware/steam-audio/releases/tag/v4.0.0]here[/url].

notes.title: Beta 17: Unreal Engine 4.24 Update
notes.notes:
We've recently updated the Steam® Audio Unreal Engine integration with the latest Beta 17 API. This version will be part-and-parcel of UE 4.24 and bolsters Steam® Audio performance with support for [url=https://steamcommunity.com/games/596420/announcements/detail/1681419156989838545]multi-threaded environmental effect simulation[/url], [url=https://steamcommunity.com/games/596420/announcements/detail/1674659226616741624]Intel® Embree[/url], and [url=https://steamcommunity.com/games/596420/announcements/detail/1681419156989664451]AMD Radeon Rays[/url].

Each of these features provide developers with significant performance boosts compared to simulating environmental effects with the built-in Steam® Audio raytracer on a single thread. Radeon Rays, which runs on any OpenCL 1.2 compatible GPU, can provide 50-150X speed-ups. Intel® Embree, which runs on the CPU, can provide speed-ups of around 20X when using recent 4-core CPUs. The built-in raytracer also benefits significantly from the new multi-threading support and its performance scales linearly with the number of threads.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/27920370/b788713414c380c689dee590d12714b2bbb73e1c.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/27920370/dd2a5b8da170b22e1350f0f444fe715980d340b3.png[/img]

[b]Figure:[/b] [i](Top) Absolute time (in milliseconds) for real-time simulation of environmental effects vs. number of threads. (Bottom) Linear scaling for real-time simulation of environmental effects vs. number of threads. Simulations were performed on Intel Xeon Platinum 8124 CPU @ 3 GHz for 32K rays, 32 bounces, and 16 sources. [/i]


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/27920370/30b33a9ee35eedc3773ded1de7dc10ded49f0093.png[/img]

[b]Figure:[/b] [i]Speedup when baking reverb using Radeon Rays vs. Embree (single-threaded) vs. Steam Audio's built-in ray tracer (single-threaded), for two scenes: Sibenik cathedral (80k triangles) and a Hangar scene from the Unity Asset Store (140k triangles). Speedups are averaged over a range of simulation settings and probe grid densities, and plotted using a logarithmic scale, shown in the graph are relative to Steam Audio's built-in ray tracer.[/i]

This is already up in Epic's UE [url=http://github.com/EpicGames/UnrealEngine/tree/4.24]main branch for 4.24[/url],  Unreal developers wanting to take early advantage of all these features can simply compile this main branch. If you prefer to grab your engine from the Epic launcher, this release will be available in the upcoming UE 4.24 Preview.

Thanks to [url=http://github.com/dyanikoglu]Doğa Can Yanıkoğlu[/url] and [url=http://github.com/muchcharles]Charles Alexander[/url] for their contributions to this Steam® Audio update and with additional features such as support for level transitions and improved geometry tagging.

[b]Full Changelist[/b]
[list][*]Updates Steam® Audio API to Beta 17 (h/t @dyanikoglu).[/*][*]Adds scene reinit on level transitions (h/t @dyanikoglu).[/*][*]Improved geometry tagging (h/t @muchcharles).[/*][*]Add support for RadeonRays and Embree raytracers.[/*][*]Better settings organization.[/*][*]Add support for multiple phonon sources.[/*][*]Ensure scene exports are reloaded between editor sessions.[/*][*]Ensure Android and 32-bit builds falls back cleanly to Phonon (if project is configured with Embree or Radeon).[/*][*]Various stability improvements.[/*][/list]
If you have any questions and/or feedback on this release, please feel free to post in the [url=https://steamcommunity.com/app/596420/discussions/]discussion forums[/url] or open an issue on [url=https://github.com/ValveSoftware/steam-audio/issues]GitHub[/url].

notes.title: Blog: Source Code Release for Steam Audio Unity Plugin
notes.notes:
我們高興地宣布我們[b]釋出了 Steam Audio Unity 外掛程式的原始碼[/b]，也就是 Steam Audio 用來在 Steam Audio API 與 Unity 之間通訊的那一部分。Steam Audio API 程式庫將繼續以二進位元檔案[url=https://valvesoftware.github.io/steam-audio/downloads.html]在 GitHub 上開放下載[/url]。

Steam Audio 的開發深深地受惠於其中[url= http://steamcommunity.com/app/596420/discussions/]活耀的社群[/url]，尤其是問題回報、功能申請，和技術貢獻的部分。釋出 Unity 外掛程式的原始碼讓社群可直接在 Steam Audio 的程式碼基底上修正問題及進行改善。如此一來便可更頻繁地改動，也不須遵循我們內部的開發週期。

Steam Audio Unity 外掛程式原始碼可從[url=https://github.com/ValveSoftware/steam-audio]我們的 GitHub 頁面上複製[/url]。存放庫中含有原生混音器和聲場定位器（Spatializer）外掛程式的 C++ 程式碼，以及遊戲引擎和編譯器整合的 C# 程式碼。組建教學也包含在原始碼中。另外，我們也更新了[url=https://github.com/ValveSoftware/steam-audio/blob/master/LICENSE.md]授權合約[/url]，以說明提交為 Steam Audio Unity 外掛程式原始碼所做出的貢獻時須遵守的規範。

如果在把玩原始碼時，有任何組建或執行外掛程式上的問題，請讓我們知道，我們將樂於提供協助！

notes.title: Blog: Source Code Release for Steam Audio Unity Plugin
notes.notes:
We're excited to announce that [b]we have released the source code for the Steam Audio Unity plugin[/b]. This is the portion of the Steam Audio source code that communicates between the Steam Audio API and Unity. The Steam Audio API libraries will continue to available as binary [url=https://valvesoftware.github.io/steam-audio/downloads.html]downloads from our GitHub page[/url].

The development of Steam Audio has benefited immensely from its [url=http://steamcommunity.com/app/596420/discussions/]active community[/url], particularly via bug reports, feature requests, and technical contributions. Releasing the Unity plugin source code will allow the community to contribute bug fixes and improvements directly to the Steam Audio code base; these contributions can be made more rapidly, and without any dependency on our development cycle.

The Steam Audio Unity plugin source code can be [url=https://github.com/ValveSoftware/steam-audio]cloned from our GitHub page[/url]. The repository contains C++ code for the native audio mixer and spatializer plugins, and C# code for the game engine and editor integration. Build instructions are included with the source code. We have also updated our [url=https://github.com/ValveSoftware/steam-audio/blob/master/LICENSE.md]license agreement[/url] to clarify the terms for submitting your contributions to the Steam Audio Unity plugin source code.

As you play around with the source code, let us know if you run into any issues with building or running the plugin, we're always happy to help!
